question: Does this real source preparation case need another whole-file request packager?

original_preparation.scope: Material discovery, impact/declaration closure, overbroad filename output, missing legacy navigation, bounded re-search, freezing files and constructing task/spec.
original_preparation.errors: Missing/old navigation and broad initial inventory are retained owner preparation costs; not HTTP or model semantic failures.

existing_capabilities.actual_specs: Both roles used source_files, task_path and max_tokens; no stable_source_path. The manifest index was side metadata, not the model source prefix.
existing_capabilities.input_precedence: A supplied stable_source_path takes precedence over source_files; the caller does not merge the two. A metadata index cannot stand in for complete source.

offline_check.conditions: Offline prepare_request only, already selected frozen files and warm filesystem. Discovery, impact analysis, path repair and closure selection are excluded.

decision.reason: Whole-file loading and source assembly already work. This evidence does not identify assembly or per-role packing as the bottleneck, so a second packager has no demonstrated saving.
decision.comparison_limit: Do not subtract millisecond offline assembly from the earlier preparation wall or call the difference saved labor. The original missing/navigation cost remains.
decision.model_candidate_correctness_adoption_and: Outside this client-preparation audit; no new candidate, compile, test or live action.

next_real_trigger: On a new real preparation task, measure bounded inventory/impact/closure stages against known owner-selected symbols and paths. Improve an existing tool only for a demonstrated mechanical bottleneck; do not auto-collect a whole repository or replace business impact selection.
